Baltimore County by the numbers

What is Baltimore County, Maryland, and how does it relate to Baltimore City?

Baltimore County is the third most populous county in Maryland, and it partly surrounds the independent city of Baltimore without including it. Towson is the county seat. Baltimore City became independent of the county on July 4, 1851, under the state's 1851 constitution, and Towson was chosen as county seat by referendum on February 13, 1854.

That split matters for sellers because the county offices described here bill and record only for properties on the county side of the line. Baltimore City runs its own tax and land records offices.

The county was founded in 1659 and named for Cecil Calvert, the second Baron Baltimore. It once included the present city plus Cecil and Harford counties. It covers 682 square miles, 598 of them land, and the 2020 census counted 854,535 residents.

What is the geography and what are the main communities in Baltimore County?

Baltimore County runs from the Chesapeake Bay shoreline in the southeast to hills along the Pennsylvania border, where the highest point reaches about 960 feet. It straddles the Piedmont in the northwest and the Atlantic Coastal Plain in the south and southeast, and the northern part is primarily rural.

Dundalk is the largest community, and the county also includes a rural north, so lot size and property type vary widely from one address to the next. The state's assessors value all of them, using the same three-year cycle.

What does the Baltimore County economy look like?

Baltimore County's major sectors are education, government and health care. A Wikipedia employer list names the Social Security Administration and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services at 14,948 jobs, Baltimore County Public Schools at 14,608, county government at 8,429 and MedStar Franklin Square Medical Center at 3,500. Black and Decker is based in Towson.

Higher education adds more local anchors: Towson University, the University of Maryland, Baltimore County in Catonsville, Goucher College, Stevenson University, and Community College of Baltimore County campuses in Catonsville, Essex and Dundalk. Baltimore County Public Schools is the county's only public school district apart from one charter school.

Transit includes the Metro SubwayLink to Owings Mills, the Light RailLink north to Hunt Valley and south through Baltimore Highlands, and MARC stops at Halethorpe, St. Denis and Martin State Airport. The county has been governed under a charter since 1956, with a county executive and a seven-member council.

How were Baltimore County values reassessed for 2026?

Baltimore County was part of the group SDAT reassessed for January 1, 2026, and its full cash value rose 12.1 percent over the three years from January 1, 2023. The notices for that group were mailed on December 30, 2025.

  • Combined value: $47.17 billion to $52.88 billion.
  • Residential value: $34.02 billion to $38.22 billion, up 12.4 percent.
  • Commercial value: $13.16 billion to $14.65 billion, up 11.3 percent.
  • Share of residential properties that increased: 85.93 percent.

Under SDAT's explanation, an increase phases in evenly over three years, while a decrease applies fully in the 2026 tax year. You can appeal within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment, and appeals start with SDAT before moving to the county appeals board and the Maryland Tax Court. SDAT keeps an office at 300 East Joppa Road, Room 602, in Towson.

How and when do you pay Baltimore County property tax?

Baltimore County issues real property tax bills on July 1, and owner-occupied homes can pay in two installments, with the first payable through September 30 and the second payable through December 31. The county's payment schedule lists July 1 and December 1 as the dates each installment is due, with September 30 and December 31 as the last days to pay without penalty or interest.

Semiannual billing is for owner-occupied residential property and small businesses, and the owner must occupy the residence for more than six months of a 12-month period. Each installment covers half of the state and county tax, half of the homestead and homeowners' credits, and half of any metropolitan charges. If a mortgage escrow pays the first installment, no December bill is issued, but the owner still has to make sure the second payment is made on time. To stay an annual payer, notify the mortgage company 60 days before the tax year.

The Office of Budget and Finance is at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call 410-887-2404 or email financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov.

What happens to an unpaid Baltimore County tax bill?

An unpaid bill in Baltimore County can lead to the property being sold at the annual June tax sale, and the county mails its notices on a fixed calendar. A missed first installment makes the account delinquent, and balances unpaid after December 31 are also delinquent.

  • February: delinquent notices are mailed, and partial payments are accepted until the end of the month.
  • End of February: deadline to apply for the Hardship Installment Payment Program to avoid a sale.
  • March 1: a Final Tax Sale notice gives 30 days to pay.
  • Around May 1: properties scheduled for sale are posted on the county website.
  • June: the annual tax sale takes place.

The county says an owner has six months from the sale date to redeem. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman describes redemption as available until a court forecloses the right, and says Baltimore County's older notices cite 12 percent per year. Because those two descriptions differ, ask the county and a lawyer which one controls your case. Partial payments do not stop interest, though they usually reduce what accrues.

What should a Baltimore County seller know about lien certificates?

A lien certificate shows the status of unpaid taxes or charges on a property account, and Baltimore County requires one before any real property transfer. The certificate costs $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application, and in most cases all unpaid taxes and charges must be paid before a transfer.

Ask for it early. The Transfer Tax Section at 410-887-2416 answers account-specific lien questions, and the Liens Section of the Clerk of the Court at 410-887-2622 handles legal liens that show on credit reports. Our Baltimore County land records guide covers the recording side of the same sale.

Does Baltimore County regulate rental properties before a sale?

Yes, every rental property in Baltimore County needs a rental license or an exemption license under County Code Section 35-5-201, and an owner must be licensed before a tenant moves in. That covers dwellings with six or fewer units, including short-term rentals, and dwellings with seven or more units.

  • Licenses last three years and can be renewed for further three-year terms.
  • Short-term rental licenses cost $300 per unit.
  • For seven or more units, an owner with fewer than three code violations in three years may use a self-certification affidavit; otherwise 10 percent of units are inspected.
  • Within one mile of Towson University's main campus, licenses may be restricted where the rental rate is 30 percent or more.

Rental Housing Registration is at 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room 216, Towson, at 410-887-6060. A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should check whether the license is current before listing.

More questions about Baltimore County, MD Property Tax Guide

When are Baltimore County property taxes due?

Bills are issued July 1, and the first installment of a semiannual bill is payable through September 30. The second installment is payable through December 31 to avoid penalty or interest.

Who can pay Baltimore County property tax in two installments?

Owner-occupied residential property and small businesses qualify. The owner must live in the home for more than six months of a 12-month period.

How much is a Baltimore County lien certificate?

The fee is $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application. The county says one is required before any real property transfer.

When is the Baltimore County tax sale?

The annual tax sale is held in June. The county mails a Final Tax Sale notice on March 1 and posts properties on its website around May 1.

How long do I have to appeal a Baltimore County assessment?

You have 45 days from the Notice of Assessment to appeal to SDAT. The appeal path then continues to the county appeals board and the Maryland Tax Court.

Do I need a rental license to sell a Baltimore County rental house?

A license is required to rent the property in the first place, so a landlord should confirm it is current before listing. Call Rental Housing Registration at 410-887-6060 with questions.

Anne Arundel County by the numbers

Where is Anne Arundel County, Maryland, and what is it like?

Anne Arundel County lies south of Baltimore on the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay, and its county seat is Annapolis, which is also the state capital. The county covers 588 square miles, but 173 of them (29 percent) are water, so shoreline and tidal creeks shape much of the housing stock.

Most of the county's borders are water. The Chesapeake Bay is to the east, the Patuxent River forms the western line with Prince George's County, and the Patapsco River forms the northern line with Baltimore County. The Magothy, Severn, South and West rivers flow into the bay from north to south. Almost all of the county sits on the Atlantic Coastal Plain, with elevation running from sea level to roughly 300 feet near the fall line.

The county was founded on April 9, 1650, and named for Lady Anne Arundell, wife of Cecilius Calvert, the second Baron Baltimore. The 2020 census counted 588,261 residents. Glen Burnie is the largest community, and others include Severna Park, Pasadena, Odenton, Crofton, Arnold, Linthicum, Severn, Gambrills, Davidsonville, Deale and Jessup.

What drives the Anne Arundel County economy and housing demand?

Anne Arundel's economy leans on federal work, defense contractors, an international airport and the state capital. A November 2014 employer list compiled on Wikipedia put Fort George G. Meade, including the National Security Agency, at 53,733 employees, with Northrop Grumman at 7,725, Anne Arundel Health System at 4,000, Southwest Airlines at 3,200 and Maryland Live! Casino at 3,000. Those are dated figures, so treat them as a snapshot of the largest employers rather than current headcounts.

The U.S. Naval Academy and St. John's College are both in Annapolis, and Anne Arundel Community College has several locations. Anne Arundel County Public Schools covers the entire county, so there is one district name on every address. Baltimore-Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport, the MTA light rail's northern portion and MARC commuter service at BWI give commuters options toward Baltimore and Washington.

County government has operated under a charter since 1965, with a county executive and a seven-member county council.

How was Anne Arundel County reassessed most recently?

Maryland's Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) reassessed Anne Arundel County for January 1, 2026, with notices mailed on December 30, 2025. The state's report on that group shows how much value moved over the three years since the last look.

Measure (Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2026)Anne Arundel County
Combined full cash value$46.52 billion to $53.53 billion (up 15.1%)
Residential value$31.23 billion to $36.24 billion (up 16.0%)
Commercial value$15.28 billion to $17.29 billion (up 13.1%)
Residential properties that rose in value98.98%

Any increase is phased in evenly over three years, while a decrease takes full effect in the 2026 tax year. An owner can appeal within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. Appeals start with SDAT, then go to the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then the Maryland Tax Court. The homestead credit limits yearly growth in taxable assessment on a principal residence, with a state cap of 10 percent and lower limits set by some local governments.

When are Anne Arundel County property tax bills due?

Anne Arundel property tax bills are mailed in July to the address on file with SDAT, and the tax is due without interest as of July 1, with a September 30 deadline. Owners of a principal residence can split the bill into two installments, due September 30 and December 31.

The county's fiscal year 2027 page, covering July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, adds a 0.87 percent service charge on the balance of the second installment. State law lets local governments add up to 1.65 percent, so the county's charge is below the ceiling. Paying the full bill by September 30 avoids the charge.

  • State rate: $0.112 per $100 of taxable assessment.
  • City of Annapolis rate: $0.738 per $100, which applies to addresses inside the city.
  • Escrowed owners who want to pay annually should notify their lender by May 1.
  • Homestead credit applications are due December 31 to take effect from July 1 of the following year.

The county rate shown on the county's pages is inconsistent between two views, so check the current rate table for your address with the office before you estimate a bill.

Which offices help with an Anne Arundel County property tax question?

The Real Property Tax Division at 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, answers billing questions, and SDAT handles values and ownership records. The division is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., its phone is (410) 222-1736, and its email is realproperty@aacounty.org.

Other useful numbers for a seller:

  • Finance Department customer service: (410) 222-1144.
  • Land Records, for deeds and liens: (410) 222-1425.
  • SDAT, for ownership and mailing address changes: (410) 974-5709.
  • Cashier's offices, including Glen Burnie: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., effective November 2, 2026. After hours, sealed check payments can go in the yellow drop-off box and are processed the next business day.

If you paid a bill for a property you no longer own, the county asks you to contact the office about a possible refund. Credit balances from adjusted bills are refunded as soon as possible.

What transfer and recordation taxes apply to a sale in Anne Arundel County?

A deed in Anne Arundel County carries a county recordation tax of $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500, and a county transfer tax of 1.0 percent up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. The county's Recordation and Transfer Tax Division collects them, and every instrument that might be subject to these taxes must be endorsed by that office before it is recorded.

Checks are payable to Anne Arundel County. State transfer tax and recording fees are handled by the Anne Arundel County Land Records Office at (410) 222-1425, and e-recording is available for land records. The county also posts claim-for-refund forms for both taxes and an affidavit form for certain transactions.

These pages do not say which side of a sale customarily pays each tax. That is set in the sales contract, so your title company should itemize it before you accept an offer.

What should waterfront sellers in Anne Arundel County know about the Critical Area?

The Critical Area is the land and water within 1,000 feet of tidal waters, and in Anne Arundel County it can change what a buyer may do with a lot.

  • The Critical Area Buffer extends 100 feet landward from tidal waters, tributary stream banks and tidal wetland boundaries, and disturbing it generally requires an approved variance.
  • Removing any tree or vegetation, including dead trees, requires an approved Vegetation Management Plan.
  • Grading disturbances over 5,000 square feet need a grading permit.
  • In limited development and resource conservation areas, impervious surface is capped at 15 to 31 percent of the site.

The county's Critical Area Planner of the Day is at the Heritage Complex, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, at (410) 222-7960. A seller with a pier, deck or bulkhead near the water should gather any permits on file before listing. The county's page does not describe any notice rule for sellers, so confirm that point with your title company.

What happens if Anne Arundel County taxes are not paid?

Unpaid Maryland property tax becomes a lien that the county can sell at a tax sale, and Anne Arundel holds its sale in June on a date set by the Controller. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman explains that the owner keeps the property after the sale, but the buyer receives a tax lien certificate and the right to foreclose if the debt stays unpaid.

Before the sale, the collector must mail notice to the owner at least 30 days before the property is first advertised, and the advertisement runs weekly for four weeks. A buyer may file a foreclosure complaint six months after the sale, or nine months for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate becomes void if no foreclosure action follows within two years. The ombudsman's page lists redemption interest of 1.5 percent per month for Anne Arundel, so waiting raises the payoff.

Limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners may qualify for help through the state's Homeowner Protection Program, and the ombudsman will meet by appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore.

More questions about Anne Arundel County, MD Property Tax Guide

When are Anne Arundel County property taxes due?

Taxes are due without interest as of July 1 and must be paid by September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and the balance by December 31.

What is the semiannual service charge in Anne Arundel County?

The county's fiscal year 2027 page lists a 0.87 percent charge on the balance of the second installment. Paying the full amount by September 30 avoids it.

How do I appeal an Anne Arundel County assessment?

File with SDAT within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. If you disagree with the result, the next steps are the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and then the Maryland Tax Court.

What are the transfer tax rates in Anne Arundel County?

The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent for transactions up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent for $1 million or more. The recordation tax is $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500.

Does the Critical Area affect selling a house near the water in Anne Arundel County?

It can. Land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters is in the Critical Area, which has a 100 foot buffer, vegetation plan rules and grading permit thresholds that a buyer may need to understand.

Can I sell an Anne Arundel County house that is behind on taxes?

Yes, but the balance must be handled at or before closing. Call the Real Property Tax Division at (410) 222-1736 for the amount owed, and act before the June tax sale.

Frederick County by the numbers

Where is Frederick County and how is it governed?

Frederick County is in north-central Maryland, in the Washington metropolitan area, with the city of Frederick as its seat. It borders Pennsylvania to the north, Carroll County to the east, Montgomery County to the south, Loudoun County, Virginia to the southwest and Washington County to the west.

At 667 square miles, with only 7.2 of them water, it is the largest Maryland county by land area. The county was founded June 10, 1748, and on December 1, 2014 it became a charter home rule government with a seven-member council and an elected county executive. Jessica Fitzwater has held that office since 2022.

Population was 271,717 in 2020, and Wikipedia gives a 2025 estimate of 302,883. Growth has been steady since the 1980s as people moved out from the Washington area.

What does the Frederick County landscape look like?

Frederick County straddles the Piedmont Plateau and the Appalachian Mountains, and its two main ridges, Catoctin Mountain and South Mountain, extend the Blue Ridge. The Middletown Valley lies between them.

That mix gives sellers very different properties:

  • City and suburban lots in and around Frederick and the county's smaller towns.
  • Valley farms in the Middletown Valley. The county leads Maryland in milk production, with dairy herds making up about a third of the state's total, though dairy farms have been closing.
  • Mountain parcels near Catoctin Mountain Park, which contains Camp David, and near the South Mountain battlefields.

Brunswick, Mount Airy, Emmitsburg and Thurmont have their own police departments, Middletown contracts with the Sheriff's Office, and fire and rescue draws on more than 450 career firefighters and about 300 volunteers across 26 corporations.

Who are the largest employers in Frederick County?

Fort Detrick is the largest employer in Frederick County, with 10,827 employees in the 2025 figures reported by Wikipedia. The next five are listed below.

EmployerEmployees (2025)
Fort Detrick10,827
Frederick County Board of Education7,433

Government, health care, research and education dominate. Riverside Research Park on the east side of Frederick hosts the National Cancer Institute's Frederick National Laboratory. With that many jobs tied to one base and its labs, the local housing market follows federal and research employment closely.

When are Frederick County property tax bills due?

Annual and first semiannual bills are due September 30, and the second semiannual installment is due December 31. Bills are mailed in July and posted online by July 1.

  • Early payment discount: 1 percent for payments received in July and one-half percent in August, on annual and semiannual bills.
  • Interest: accrues on unpaid accounts from October 1 at 1 percent per month.
  • Supplemental bills: mailed in August for June transfers and state credits issued after the July billing. Supplemental and revised bills are due 30 days from issue.
  • Postmark rule: USPS payments postmarked by the last calendar day of the month are credited as of the postmark date. Electronic payments must be entered by midnight on the last day.

The county says that failing to receive a bill does not excuse payment. Mortgage companies do not receive bills; they use an electronic file. Homeowners who escrow must send new construction bills to their lender, because those go only to the owner.

Where do you pay Frederick County property tax?

The Frederick County Treasury Department is at 30 North Market Street in Frederick, open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, and its number is 301-600-1111. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and cards in person.

Card payments are processed through a vendor with a 2.5 percent fee, and the county says it receives none of that fee. The mailing address is the Treasury Department at 30 N. Market St., Frederick, MD 21701. Lenders can use a mass payment option through the billing office.

The county's Treasury page also offers Lien Certificate and Tax Status Report requests. Ordering one before closing shows what tax, if any, is still open.

What rates and local taxes apply in Frederick County?

Unincorporated Frederick County had a real property rate of 1.1100 per $100 of assessed value in fiscal 2025, and the same rate is shown for fiscal 2026. The rate was 1.0600 from fiscal 2022 to 2024.

State tables list a Frederick County transfer tax of 0.0 percent and a recordation tax figure of $7.00 for fiscal 2025 and 2026. Each municipality also levies its own district tax for services such as streets, trash removal and police. Homestead credit caps vary by municipality from 0 percent to 10 percent.

The county page lists these relief programs:

  • Senior Tax Credit: for owners 65 or older who meet income limits, equal to 20 percent of net county real property taxes.
  • Deferral program: for owners of at least five years who are 65 or older or totally disabled and meet income limits. Deferred amounts become a lien at 3 percent annual interest.
  • Homestead Tax Credit: limits yearly taxable assessment increases on a principal residence, applied automatically after 12 months of residence. Call SDAT at 301-815-5350.
  • Homeowner's Property Tax Credit: income based for all ages, with applications due by September of the tax year.

How can you appeal a Frederick County assessment?

Frederick County owners appeal to the Supervisor of Assessments within 45 days of the notice date, then to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days, then to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days. Both the board and the Tax Court have no filing fee.

Notices come about every three years. In the two years between, a petition for review is due by the first working day after January 1. Hearings at the first level can be written, by phone, by video or in person. If you bought a house transferred between January 1 and June 30, you can appeal within 60 days of the transfer once the deed is recorded.

What if Frederick County tax goes unpaid or the house needs repairs?

Frederick County sells tax liens online, and the state's 2026 schedule lists the county on May 11. An owner can redeem until the Circuit Court forecloses the right.

The county says an owner keeps possession during redemption. Redemption without added expenses such as legal fees is possible during the first four months for a non-owner-occupied property and the first seven months for an owner-occupied one. The certificate interest rate is 8 percent a year. Call 301-600-1111 for the redemption amount.

Rental condition is a separate matter. The county replaced its Minimum Livability Code with the 2024 International Property Maintenance Code, effective June 6, 2026, and the Division of Housing at 401 Sagner Avenue enforces it on complaint. What is Prince George's County, Maryland, and why does its geography matter for a tax bill?

Prince George's County sits on the eastern side of Washington, D.C., and covers about 499 square miles, of which 483 are land. The Patuxent River forms its eastern edge, and only South County touches the Potomac.

Residents and planners talk about five informal regions: North County, Central County, the Rural Tier, the Inner Beltway and South County. U.S. Route 50 is the broad line between north and south. The county seat is Upper Marlboro, and the county was created in 1696 from parts of Charles and Calvert counties.

Geography shows up on the bill in two ways. A house inside an incorporated city, such as Bowie, carries a municipal tax and gets a reduced county rate. A house in unincorporated land pays the county rate in full. Anyone selling should check which one applies before reading a bill.

Who lives and works in Prince George's County?

The 2020 census counted 967,201 people in the county, and the 2025 estimate is 970,374, which makes it the second most populous county in Maryland after Montgomery. The county has had a charter form of government since 1970, with nine council districts plus two at-large seats.

Federal employment shapes the local economy more than most counties. The figures below are 2021 employer counts reported on the county's Wikipedia entry.

For a seller, this means many owners have jobs tied to federal posts and transfers. A reassignment can force a sale on a short clock, which is one reason owners here look for a quick closing.

How do roads and rail connect the county's neighborhoods?

The county has 15 Washington Metro stations, and four of them are line ends: Greenbelt, New Carrollton, Largo and Branch Avenue. MARC commuter trains add five Camden Line stops and three Penn Line stops.

  • 28 miles of the Capital Beltway (I-495) run through the county.
  • An 11.5-mile stretch of the Baltimore-Washington Parkway lies inside its borders.
  • The Intercounty Connector opened in 2012.
  • The Purple Line is described as slated to open in 2027.

Distance to a Metro or MARC station is one of the first things a buyer checks, so it also affects how fast a house sells on the open market.

When is the Prince George's County property tax bill due?

The county issues bills every July, and full payment is due September 30. Late payments pick up interest and a penalty, and missing a bill does not excuse the owner.

Owner-occupied homes with a bill marked Principal Residence can pay in two equal parts, the first by September 30 and the second by December 31. Maryland lets local governments add a service charge of up to 1.65% to the second half, according to the state assessments department.

The county's Tax Facts guide gives the late charge as 1.67% per month. The tax year runs July 1 to June 30. Treat that figure as a reason to pay on time rather than a number to plan around.

What rates make up a Prince George's County bill?

The county's own formula is simple: divide the assessment by 100, multiply by the rate, then add any charges. The guide also gives a constant yield rate of $0.9591 for tax year 2026 and a certified unincorporated assessable base of $86.5 billion.

Extra charges can appear on the same bill. Front Foot Benefit covers sewer or water pipes laid in the street (WSSC, 301-206-8032). Solid Waste Service pays for trash and waste programs (Department of the Environment, 301-952-7630). A tax lien charge appears when taxes or fines are in arrears.

How does a reassessment change what an owner pays?

The State Department of Assessments and Taxation sets values, and it reassesses each property every three years. The January 1, 2026 cycle raised residential values in Prince George's County by 10.3% compared with January 1, 2023, and notices went out on December 30, 2025.

Increases are phased in evenly over three years, and decreases take full effect in the 2026 tax year. Homestead and Homeowners' credits are also run by the state, and the county's own credits are listed on its Property Tax Credits page.

Disagreements start with the state assessments department, then go to the county Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then to the Maryland Tax Court. For a dwelling, the appeal board must hold a hearing within 120 days after receiving the request, unless the owner asks for a delay.

Treasury Customer Service at 301-952-4030 handles questions, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The counter is in the Wayne K. Curry Administration Building, 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo.

  • Online through the Tax Inquiry site: $1.50 for an e-check, $3.95 for a Visa debit card, 2.45% for other cards.

  • A 24-hour walk-up slot at the front entrance takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks, and a drive-up drop box opens at the end of September and December.

Real property taxes still unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the county's annual tax sale. That sale turns a late bill into a lien held by a third party, so it is a real deadline.

Owners behind on taxes often find that a conventional listing is difficult, because lenders and title companies need the balance cleared at closing. A cash buyer can sometimes pay the arrears at settlement out of the price. Ask the Treasury Division for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

What does a seller pay when the deed is recorded?

Maryland charges transfer and recordation taxes on a sale, and the rates differ by county. A 2026 staff table at the Maryland General Assembly lists Prince George's County at a 1.4% transfer tax and a recordation tax of $2.75 per $500 of consideration, both unchanged from fiscal 2022 through fiscal 2027. Which side pays, and how the split is written, is set in the contract of sale. Confirm the exact amounts with the title company, since municipal and state add-ons differ by deal.

The county's Office of Homeland Security code compliance staff enforce housing, zoning and rental rules. Inspectors act on complaints or cleanup sweeps and issue a Notice of Violation, a Civil Citation or both, with a deadline to fix the problem.

  • A single-family rental needs a county license, valid for two years, unless the city or town licenses it instead. Bowie is among the municipalities the county does not license.
  • A license is refused when an inspector finds life-safety violations, including unpermitted construction or an illegal conversion.
  • Landlords who use a pre- or post-settlement occupancy agreement between buyer and seller are exempt from the license requirement.

A house with open citations or unpermitted work can lose bids, so a seller who cannot fix them in time may prefer an as-is sale.

What must a Prince George's County seller disclose?

A seller of a one- to four-unit home must give the buyer a disclosure or a disclaimer statement on or before signing the contract, under Maryland Real Property Code section 10-702. The disclaimer form says the home is sold as-is, apart from known latent defects.

Several sales are exempt, including bank sales after foreclosure, sheriff and tax sales, and transfers by fiduciaries in estates and trusts. A buyer who did not get the statement in time can rescind within five days after receiving it, and the right cannot be waived in the contract.

Full payment is due September 30, and bills go out each July. Owner-occupied homes marked Principal Residence can split it into September 30 and December 31 installments.

Where is the Prince George's County Treasury Division?

The customer counter is at 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo, MD 20774, open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. Call 301-952-4030 for help.

Can I pay Prince George's County property tax with cash?

No, the county says cash is not accepted at its counter. It takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks in person, plus cards and e-checks online with fees.

When does the Prince George's County tax sale happen?

Taxes unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the annual tax sale. Contact Treasury before then for a payoff figure.

A 2026 General Assembly staff table lists 1.4% for the county, with a $2.75 recordation rate per $500. The state adds its own 0.5% transfer tax, so confirm totals with the title company.

Who sets my assessment in Prince George's County?

The Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation does. Reassessment happens every three years, and the January 1, 2026 cycle raised residential values by 10.3%.

Does Bowie get its rental license from the county?

No. The county says Bowie is among the municipalities it does not license, so landlords apply with the city.

Where is Charles County and what is its layout?

Charles County sits in Southern Maryland, with La Plata as the county seat and Waldorf as its largest community. It is bordered by Prince George's County to the north, Calvert and St. Mary's counties to the east and southeast, and several Virginia counties across the Potomac.

The county covers 643 square miles, but only 458 of them are land. The other 185 square miles, about 29 percent, are water, which is why creeks, swamps and shoreline show up in so many property descriptions. Nanjemoy Creek and Zekiah Swamp are two of the named features.

Charles County was created in 1658 and named for Charles Calvert, the third Baron Baltimore. Its population was 166,617 in the 2020 census, and the 2025 estimate cited by Wikipedia is 176,593, up 6.0 percent.

What towns and areas do Charles County sellers deal with?

Most sellers here fall into one of four settings: Waldorf, La Plata, Indian Head or the rural south and west. Each has its own buyer pool and its own tax picture.

  • Waldorf: a census-designated place about 23 miles south-southeast of Washington, D.C. It had 81,410 residents in 2020, up from fewer than 5,000 in 1980, largely because of the planned community of St. Charles that began after a 1970 federal loan package. U.S. Route 301 is its main commercial road and Maryland Route 5 starts there.
  • La Plata: the county seat, where the April 28, 2002 tornado (rated F-4) destroyed much of downtown and killed three people.
  • Indian Head: a town tied to the naval installation on the Potomac, which is the county's largest employer.
  • Rural Charles: places such as Nanjemoy, Port Tobacco Village, Newburg and Bryantown, where lots are larger, wells and septic are common, and water is never far away.

The Naval Surface Warfare Center and Naval Support Facility Indian Head is the largest employer in Charles County, followed by the public school system. The table below uses the 2022 employer ranking reported by Wikipedia.

Four MTA commuter bus routes (901, 903, 905 and 907) run between Waldorf and downtown Washington, D.C., and federal work, professional services and health care are the main jobs for commuters. A household that relies on a federal paycheck or a base contract may need to move on a fixed schedule, which is one reason some owners want a fast sale.

How is property tax billed in Charles County?

The Charles County Treasurer bills and collects real property tax, and full-year bills go out in July. Owners of a principal residence can split the bill: the first installment is due September 30, and the second, with the applicable service charge, is due December 31.

Supplemental bills for new construction or improvements are generally mailed in October (three-quarter year), January (half year) and April (quarter year). If a mortgage company pays your tax, send it your bill and check your escrow analysis to be sure it was paid.

  • Office: 200 Baltimore Street, La Plata, MD 20646. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2607.
  • Phone: 301-645-0685
  • Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Waldorf payment center closes from 11:15 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. each day.
  • Assessment questions: the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) sets values; the county page gives 301-932-2440 for questions.

The county page says delinquent properties may be offered at the annual tax sale held each May. The state tax sale schedule for 2026 lists Charles County on May 12.

What property tax rates apply in Charles County towns?

A house in unincorporated Charles County carried a total real property rate of 1.2050 per $100 of assessed value in the fiscal 2025 state table, and towns add their own rate on top. The figures below come from the Department of Legislative Services table built from SDAT data.

The county special rate is 0.0640 in the unincorporated area and in the municipalities listed, and the table shows Port Tobacco at a total of 1.2450. The rate is applied to the taxable assessment divided by 100, so a bill is easy to check with a calculator.

Maryland's state tables also list a Charles County transfer tax of 0.5 percent and a recordation tax figure of $5.00 for fiscal 2025 and $7.00 for fiscal 2026. Ask the title company for the exact charges on your closing statement.

What credits and appeal rights can reduce a Charles County bill?

Charles County lists several credits, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation reviews the applications. They include the Homestead Tax Credit, the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (income based), a senior tax credit and an exemption for 100 percent disabled veterans. The county page also lists credits for a perpetual conservation easement, for the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer and for volunteer emergency responders.

If you think the value is too high, the state appeal path applies in Charles County as it does elsewhere in Maryland.

  1. File with the Supervisor of Assessments within 45 days of the notice date, online with the control number on the notice or on paper.
  2. If you disagree with the result, appeal to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days of the Supervisor's final notice. There is no fee.
  3. Take the case to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order. Hearings there are in person and start fresh.

A buyer who purchases a house transferred between January 1 and June 30 can also appeal within 60 days of the transfer date, provided the deed has been recorded.

What does flood risk mean for a Charles County house?

Charles County tries to keep its floodplain open so water can spread out and move downstream, and a house inside a mapped Special Flood Hazard Area is treated differently from one outside it. The county's floodplain page states plainly that homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage and that residents can buy a National Flood Insurance Program policy through an insurance agent.

With 29 percent of the county's total area in water, owners near the Potomac, creeks and swamps should expect a buyer's lender to ask about flood zone status. Check the FEMA map for the parcel before listing, and have any flood insurance paperwork ready. Flood status can also affect the price a buyer offers.

What happens if Charles County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid property tax in Maryland becomes a lien, and the county can sell that lien at public auction. The owner keeps the house, but the buyer gains the right to collect and eventually to ask a court to foreclose.

The Maryland tax sale ombudsman's page explains the main steps:

  • The collector mails a notice at least 30 days before the property is first advertised, and the listing runs weekly for four weeks.
  • An owner can redeem at any time until a court finally forecloses the right to redeem, and costs grow the longer the owner waits.
  • The buyer may file for foreclosure after six months, or nine months for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate is void if no case is filed within two years.

When a house is sold before that point, the title company normally pays the tax from the sale proceeds. The ombudsman's office can be reached at 410-767-4994, and its Homeowner Protection Program helps limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners.

Where is Carroll County, and how is it laid out?

  • A pending appeal or tax credit application does not change the due date.

How does the Carroll County tax sale work?

The county sells liens on unpaid real estate tax in an online sale run through RealAuction each June. For 2025 the notice said proceedings started April 1, and the sale was held June 30.

Starting May 1, delinquent taxes must be paid by cash, certified check or money order, and additional fees apply. Owners who wait until late April or May lose the card and online options.

Paying the current year does not protect you from legal action for unpaid prior years, according to the county. A Homeowner Protection Program page is linked from the Collections Office, so ask about eligibility if you are close to the sale.

Qualifications differ, so call before assuming you are eligible.

Maryland Route 140 is the main road, running from Baltimore through Westminster toward Taneytown. Route 97 is the most direct way south toward Washington, and Routes 27 and 31 link nearby towns. Westminster has no inter-county bus or rail service to Baltimore County, so most residents drive.

The county sits on a line between humid subtropical and hot-summer humid continental climates. Westminster averages about 43 inches of precipitation and 20 inches of snow a year, which puts steady demands on roofs, gutters and heating systems.

Westminster itself was founded in 1764 and incorporated in 1818, and Corbit's Charge was fought on its streets on June 28, 1863. Its older downtown housing is a very different product from the newer subdivisions around Eldersburg.

What should a Carroll County seller do about tax at closing?

  2. Ask the Collections Office for a payoff and for the status of any lien.

Where is Calvert County, and what does its shape mean for homeowners?

Calvert County fills a peninsula in Southern Maryland, with the Chesapeake Bay on the east and the Patuxent River on the west. Prince Frederick is the county seat, and the county is part of the Washington metropolitan area.

Total area is about 345 square miles, but water covers roughly 38% of that, which makes Calvert the smallest county in Maryland by land area. Five islands, including Solomons Island and Broomes Island, belong to the county.

That much shoreline shapes the housing market. A waterfront cottage in Chesapeake Beach and a ranch house on a wooded lot near Prince Frederick can both sit in the same county and have very little in common when it comes to insurance, septic and maintenance.

What drives the Calvert County economy?

Government, schools, health care and energy account for the largest payrolls. The county's 2019 employer list names Calvert County Public Schools with 2,147 employees, the county government with 1,269, Calvert Memorial Hospital with 1,225, Constellation with 822 and Walmart with 460.

The Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant and the Cove Point LNG Terminal are both on the western shore at Lusby. Tourism is centered on Solomons, Chesapeake Beach and North Beach, and the Chesapeake Beach Resort and Spa employs 239 people.

Farming shifted in the mid-1990s away from tobacco toward fruit, vegetables and meat. Many residents commute toward Washington, and the county's median household income is among the highest in the country, which keeps demand for houses steady even when a particular property needs work.

Calvert's total full cash value rose 9.0% in the 2026 reassessment, from about $5.07 billion to $5.52 billion, and residential value rose 8.8%. The state's Group 2 review last looked at the county in 2023.

The state caps taxable increases for owner-occupied homes under the homestead credit, and Calvert's cap is 10% a year effective July 1, 2026, higher than the caps in most nearby counties. That means a Calvert homeowner who has applied for the credit has less protection than one in Baltimore or Cecil, where the cap is 4%. Increases in assessed value are phased in over three years either way.

When does Calvert County bill property tax, and what does the Treasurer's Office handle?

The tax year runs July 1 through June 30, and owners of a principal residence can pay in two installments: September 30 and December 31. The second installment carries a service charge, and the county page does not state the amount.

If you have not received a bill by August 31, you can ask the Treasurer's Office for a duplicate. New construction is billed on a half-year basis from January 1 through June 30.

The Homeowner Protection Program can take a qualifying owner out of the tax sale process for three years. The county page lists a principal residence, an assessed value of $300,000 or less, household income of $60,000 or less, and non-dwelling assets of $200,000 or less.

For a seller, these programs matter in two ways. They may reduce what you owe before closing, and they can slow a tax sale long enough to list or sell the house without a lien deadline hanging over you.

Calvert County charges a building excise tax on new residential construction, and it follows the property as a lien. A new single-family detached house carries a total of $12,950, with $4,550 due at permit and $4,200 on each of the next two tax bills.

The county schedule lists other totals: $10,325 for a single-family attached unit, $9,050 for a manufactured home and $7,750 for an apartment. Because later installments appear on the regular tax bill, a buyer of a newly built home should ask whether any installments remain unpaid.

Calvert enforces this tax like real property tax, with the same priority, interest and penalties for lien purposes. If you are selling a house built in the last two or three years, ask the Treasurer's Office what remains.

How do roads, water and weather affect a Calvert County sale?

Route 4 and Route 2 meet at Sunderland and run together as Route 2-4, Solomons Island Road, through Prince Frederick, St. Leonard and Lusby. Route 260 runs southeast to Chesapeake Beach, Route 231 heads west to the Benedict Bridge, and the Governor Thomas Johnson Bridge carries Route 4 into St. Mary's County.

The climate is humid subtropical, with summers that are hot and humid and winters that are mild to chilly. Prince Frederick averages about 36 degrees in January and 78 in July. Bay proximity moderates temperatures, and a house here sees a full range of heat, humidity and winter cold on its roof and siding.

Calvert Cliffs State Park protects the exposed Calvert Formation on the western shore, and the cliffs are a known fossil collecting site.

What should you do first if you are selling a Calvert County house with tax due?

A Calvert owner who disagrees with an assessment must appeal to the state assessment office within 45 days of the notice date. The 2026 notices were mailed December 30, 2025.

Cecil County was organized in 1674 and named for Cecil Calvert, the second Baron Baltimore. It was an early trading and shipping center, and the Principio Furnace exported pig iron.

Elkton sits at the head of navigation on the Elk River. Swedish mariners and fishermen settled the area in 1694 as Head of Elk, and the town was incorporated in 1787. In the 1920s and 1930s, Elkton was known as the elopement capital of the East Coast because of Maryland's looser marriage rules, with thousands of weddings a year.

Where is Dorchester County and how big is it?

Dorchester County is on Maryland's Mid-Eastern Shore, with Cambridge as the county seat and largest city. It is the largest Maryland county by area and the least densely populated.

The county covers 983 square miles, and 442 of them (45 percent) are water. It borders the Choptank River to the north, Talbot and Caroline counties, Wicomico County, Sussex County in Delaware and the Chesapeake Bay on the west. Much of it is marsh, forest and farmland, and the county's own slogan is The Heart of Chesapeake Country.

The county was formed in 1669 and named for the Earl of Dorset. Harriet Tubman was born here. The 2020 census counted 32,531 people, with a median age of 45.1, and the 2025 estimate is 33,628.

What is Cambridge like for a home seller?

Cambridge sits on the south bank of the Choptank River at about 20 feet above sea level, and it had 13,096 residents in 2020. It was incorporated in 1793, and part of its downtown was declared a historic district in 1990.

Canning built the town. Phillips Packing Company employed up to 10,000 people at its peak and closed completely by the early 1960s, which left lasting unemployment. The Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay resort opened in 2002 with 400 rooms, a golf course and a marina, and Cambridge became a Maryland Main Street community on July 1, 2003.

  • U.S. Route 50 runs through the city, and the eastern stretch is called Sunburst Highway.
  • Cambridge-Dorchester Airport is a county-owned general aviation field southeast of town with a 4,477 foot runway.
  • The Cambridge Historic District covers Wards I and III in the northwest, and the Pine Street Neighborhood Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Of the city's 6,464 housing units, 13.9 percent were vacant at the 2020 census. Owners of a vacant house there still owe the same tax and carry the same upkeep.

What drives the Dorchester County economy?

Water and farmland have long been the base of the Dorchester County economy. Many residents were historically watermen and farmers, and the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries supply crabs, oysters and many fish species to commercial and recreational fishermen.

Horn Point Laboratory in the Cambridge area is home to the largest oyster hatchery on the East Coast. A 4.3 megawatt solar farm in Cambridge supplies about 40 percent of the power for the National Aquarium in Baltimore.

The county works under a charter home rule government with a five-member council. We did not find a current ranked employer list on an official page, so we leave one out rather than guess. With only about 33,600 residents countywide, a seller works with a small local buyer pool.

How much of Dorchester County is in a flood zone?

About 55 percent of the land in Dorchester County lies in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, and nearly 75 percent of it is below 20 feet in elevation. Those figures come from the county's 2022 Flood Mitigation Plan update.

Church Creek, Eldorado and Galestown are fully within storm surge zones, according to the plan. If your house is near the water, expect a buyer to ask about elevation, flood insurance and past claims. Gather those records before you list.

How is Dorchester County property tax billed and collected?

Dorchester County bills in July, and the annual bill and the first semiannual installment are due September 30, with the second installment due December 31. The county collects real property tax for every municipality in the county.

Payment options listed by the county include the online Tax and Utility Bill portal run through a vendor, mail, and an in-person visit to the County Office Building at 501 Court Lane in Cambridge. The county main number is 410-228-1700, and the state's list of billing offices shows the Department of Finance at 410-228-4343. The county's page for the office notes closures for Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day and Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

After the due dates pass, unpaid accounts accrue interest and a penalty, and the lien can move toward the county's tax sale. Ask the finance office for a payoff figure on the exact day you plan to close, since interest runs monthly.

What are the tax rates in Dorchester County and Cambridge?

Unincorporated Dorchester County had a real property rate of 1.0000 per $100 in fiscal 2025, and the county rate in the state's newer table rises to 1.0300 for fiscal 2026. Towns add their own rate.

Cambridge0.92670.80961.7363
Hurlock0.91790.72031.6382

The same state tables list a county transfer tax of 0.75 percent and a recordation tax figure of $5.00. These are the amounts to expect on a closing statement, but the title company calculates the actual charge from the deed and price.

A house in Cambridge therefore carries a much higher combined rate than a similar house in the open county. If you are choosing between listing in town and holding a rural parcel, compare the two bills first.

How does the Dorchester County tax sale work?

Dorchester County runs its tax sale online, and in 2025 bidding opened at noon on June 16 and closed at noon on June 17. The state's 2026 schedule lists Dorchester County on May 19, so confirm the date with the finance office.

  • The 2025 sale covered unpaid taxes and fees for tax years 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025.
  • Bidders registered online, and the registration fee was $50.
  • An owner could stop a sale by paying in full by 4:00 p.m. on June 12, 2025.
  • Owners also owe a $50 advertising fee per property and interest as the law provides.

State guidance adds that owners can redeem until a court forecloses, and that a buyer can ask for foreclosure after six months, or nine months for an owner-occupied home. The certificate is void if no foreclosure case is filed in two years.

What can you appeal or claim on a Dorchester County property?

Dorchester County owners use the same state appeal ladder as everyone in Maryland, and the first step has a 45 day deadline from the notice date. SDAT normally reassesses property every three years and mails a Notice of Assessment.

After the Supervisor of Assessments, an owner can go to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days, then to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order. In the years between reassessments, a petition for review is due by the first working day after January 1. A buyer of a house transferred between January 1 and June 30 has 60 days from the transfer, once the deed is recorded.

More questions about Dorchester County, MD Property Tax Guide

When are Dorchester County property taxes due?

The annual bill and first installment are due September 30, and the second installment is due December 31. Bills are mailed in July. Interest and a penalty start after those dates, so pay by the deadline or ask for a payoff figure.

How much of Dorchester County is in a floodplain?

About 55 percent of the county's land lies in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, according to the county's 2022 Flood Mitigation Plan. Nearly 75 percent of the land is under 20 feet in elevation.

What is the property tax rate in Cambridge, Maryland?

In the fiscal 2025 state table, Cambridge totals 1.7363 per $100 of assessed value, made of a 0.9267 county rate and a 0.8096 town rate. Unincorporated Dorchester County totals 1.0000. Check the current year's rate before you rely on these numbers.

Can I sell a Dorchester County house before the tax sale?

Yes, if you pay the tax and fees before the cutoff the house comes off the sale list, and a closing can pay the balance from proceeds. In 2025 the payment deadline was June 12 at 4:00 p.m., so ask the finance office for the current date.

Is the Dorchester County transfer tax 0.75 percent?

The state's local tax table lists a 0.75 percent transfer tax for Dorchester County in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Who pays, and any exemptions, depend on the contract and the deed, so confirm the amount with the title company.
